messages:
Cara: quick heads-up — after the kernel-selector tweak merged in yesterday, our /chat route saw a p95 jump. I captured traces/profiler output below. thinking SLO-driven token-budget scaling by route/tier might be the fastest mitigation before we consider reverting. any quick thoughts?

Devon: numbers pls — how big is the jump and across which tiers?

Cara: baseline before change: p95 ~85ms (seq distribution median 64 tokens). after: p95 ~150ms for /chat free, ~120ms for standard, enterprise unchanged (~88ms). KV cache hit-rate dropped from ~92% -> ~74% on free route. throughput steady. sample profiler (top lines):
```
kernel_selector: selected_small_matmul x80%, selected_fused_attn x20%
gpu_util: 82%
cpu_wait_for_batch_ms: p50 2ms p95 28ms
microbatch_wait_ms: p50 1ms p95 40ms
kv_lookup_ms: p95 increased 3x
batch_size_dist: mode 6 -> shifted to 3 after change
```
I suspect kernel selection causes smaller microbatches and more KV thrash.

PerfBot: automated perf run #2026-03-17-1
- route: /chat (free)
- traffic: 10k rps sample
- p50: 42ms p95: 152ms p99: 420ms
- avg batch size: 3.2 (was 6.1)
- kv_hit_rate: 73.9%
- cost delta: +12%
(see /perf/runs/2026-03-17-1) :bar_chart:

Siva: this reads like the batcher is forming smaller batches after the new kernels changed token-latency profile. For a fast mitigation propose: dynamic token-budget target by route+tier with age-aware queueing. simple rule: target_token_budget(route,tier) = clamp(base(route) * tier_scale(tier) * slack_factor, min, max). e.g. base(/chat)=64, tier_scale = {free:0.6, standard:1.0, enterprise:2.0} -> targets: free=38 ~ 64*0.6, standard=64, enterprise=128. slack_factor defaults 1.0 but can be lowered to prioritize latency.

Siva: queue policy: age-priority with token-aware preemption. items aged >50ms get bumped in front even if they don't fill target. this keeps p95 in check for long tails.

Henry: +1 on age-priority. also KV cache behavior note: the kernel change altered KV access patterns (we now hit different memory layout which increased L2 misses on some devices). For premium routes we should increase local KV capacity and pin popular prefixes to avoid eviction churn while we tune batcher.

Anna: proposed experiment plan:
1) create canary config (5% traffic) with token budgets: free=40, standard=96, enterprise=192 and age-priority queueing enabled.
2) monitor p95, p50, batch_size_dist, kv_hit_rate, cost delta for 2 hours.
3) if p95 improves <10% and cost delta <5%, ramp to 25% and re-evaluate.

Anna: rbatchctl snippets to apply canary:
```
rbatchctl set-config --route /chat --tier free --token-budget 40 --queue-policy age-priority --canary 0.05
rbatchctl set-config --route /chat --tier standard --token-budget 96 --queue-policy age-priority --canary 0.05
rbatchctl set-config --route /chat --tier enterprise --token-budget 192 --queue-policy age-priority --canary 0.05
```

Devon: what metrics should SRE/observability dashboards highlight during the canary? p95, kv_hit_rate, avg_batch_size, microbatch_wait_ms, gpu_occupancy, cost_per_1k_tokens?

Cara: exactly. add: queue_age_p99 and prefix_hotset_evictions. alert if p95 > baseline*1.15 or kv_hit_rate drops >10pp.

Henry: I'll spin profiler on the same canary hosts and capture kernel selection histograms + memory counters (L2 misses). need a trace id to tag logs.

Cara: trace id: trace-20260317-42. I'll attach the traces to the canary run and post updates. also toggling a small increase to KV pin threshold for enterprise only during canary.

PerfBot: canary started (id=canary-2026-03-17-8)
- initial 30m snapshot: p95 reduced to 98ms on canary traffic (free), avg_batch_size increased to 5.1, kv_hit_rate recovered to 88.5%, cost delta +3.2%
- note: kernel_selector now picks fused_attn more often in canary which seems to yield better microbatching behavior.

Cara: this looks promising. next steps: keep canary for 4h, collect full histograms, then propose a 25% ramp if sustained. I'll file a short RFC with config defaults and the formula Siva suggested. tagging @eng-runtime @eng-ml for visibility. :rocket:

Devon: ping me if you want help with dashboards / alerts.

Anna: I'll own the rollout playbook and add rollback steps and cost thresholds.

Cara: thanks all — will update thread with RFC link and final numbers.
